subject: Remembering Selected Items across interactive UI updates

messages.author: 7abbca01b0fa5d25
messages.subject: Remembering Selected Items across interactive UI updates
parts:
Dear all, I am trying to develop an interactive UI where depending on the user that log in the app, different Orders made of different Samples will populate the UI for the user to make a selection. My current layout uses a selectInput() widget to display the orders and the samples for the selected orders populate a checkboxGroupInput() widget. This works without a glitch. My goal is to somehow, let the user select samples across different selected orders (i.e. the user can go to the second order, select 3 items, then to the 4th order and pick two). What I am unable to do thus far is to create some object that would remember the selected items when the user change orders. I would also like to select the samples for a given order that have been previously selected if the user goes back to a previously seen Order. I have almost successfully achieve that goal using a reactiveValues() but it fails for different reason... 1) when a user goes back to a previously selected order, the associated list of samples get wiped out. 

Ok, this might be all a bit cryptic but here is a sample app that describe exactly the problem. 

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks a bunch.

library(shiny)

## ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
    titlePanel("Rembembering Selection"),
    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            helpText(h5("This app should display items based on the selected origin
                         and remember what had been selected")),
            br(),
            helpText(h5("Select a sample from the list below then select items")),
            uiOutput("orderSelector"),
            uiOutput("sampleSelector")
            
            ),
        mainPanel(
            tableOutput('df'),
            textOutput('text1')
            )
        )
    ))


## server.R
library(shiny)

## Randomly create a list of Orders associated with sets of samples
order.ids <- sample(LETTERS,sample(3:7,1))
samples <- lapply(order.ids,function(s)rep(paste0("Sample-",s,".id",sample(1:1000,sample(3:15,1)))))
names(samples) <- paste0("Order-",order.ids)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    ## Provide the user a drop down with his order names
    output$orderSelector <- renderUI({
        selectInput('order','Select an order to display the associatd samples',names(samples))
    })

    ## Return an the vector of samples
    items <- reactive({ samples[[input$order]] })

    ## Create the checkbox widget for the user to make a selection
    output$sampleSelector <- renderUI({
        if (length(exps()[[input$order]]) != 0){
            selected <- exps()[[input$order]]
        } else {
            selected <- NULL
        }
        checkboxGroupInput("samples",
                           "Choose sample(s) for further analysis",
                           items(),
                           selected)
    })
    
    ## Create a reactiveValues to store the selections
    values <- reactiveValues()
    exps <- reactive({
        if (length(input$order)!= 0){
            values[[input$order]] <- input$samples
            return(values)
        }
    })

    ## Return usefull info for development
    output$text1 <- renderText({
        if (length(exps()[[input$order]]) != 0){
            paste("Selected Samples in order",input$order,paste0(exps()[[input$order]],collapse=':'))
        } else {
            paste("No Sample Selected for",input$order)
        }
    })

    ## Return a data frame of the number of item selected per order
    output$df <- renderTable({
        if (length(exps()) != 0){
            data.frame(exp=names(exps()),num=sapply(exps(),length))
        }
    })  
})

messages.subject: Re: Remembering Selected Items across interactive UI updates
parts:
Ok, thanks to the app gallery, you guys did a great job of putting some cool code that are super great to learn the intricacies of shiny, but bottom line, I figure out an easy way to save the state of a selection through changes in the UI.

here is the bits that does the magic. It uses a reactiveValues() and an observer({}) block to watch and update the state of the reactiveValues(). Not really easy to pick up at first but I make sense when you think about it. here it is (I would be very happy to get comments on whether this is the shiny way or not...)

    ## Remember the selected samples
    exps <- reactiveValues()
    observe({
        ## If no orders are selected, just return, whipping off the values in the exps list
        if (is.null(input$samples)){
            if (!is.null(input$order)){
                exps[[input$order]] <- NULL
            }
            return()
        }
        isolate({
            exps[[input$order]] <- input$samples
        })
    })
